userStories.title: Store a NOTE memory item through POST /memory
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Store validated note-shaped memory with slug-based supersession through the existing REST write path.

**Motivation** — MemoryItem is a subject/predicate/object triple in the kinds FACT, DECISION, PREFERENCE, CONSTRAINT and INCIDENT_PATTERN. That fits decisions, not a Markdown note with a type and a description (#376).

**Approach** — A note is a `MemoryItem` with `kind: 'NOTE'`, `subject` = slug, `predicate` = type, `object` = Markdown body, `description` = the index line. The limits are nax's own (nax `packages/nax-agent/src/memory/types.ts`) so a note round-trips: `MEMORY_NOTE_SLUG_RE = /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$/`, `MEMORY_NOTE_TYPES = ['user', 'feedback', 'project', 'reference']`, `MEMORY_NOTE_BODY_MAX_BYTES = 8192` (UTF-8 bytes of `object`), `MEMORY_NOTE_DESCRIPTION_MAX_CHARS = 200`. They live in a new `apps/api/src/memory/memory-note.ts` with `noteFieldError(input: { kind: string; subject: string; predicate: string; object?: string; description?: string }): 'subject' | 'predicate' | 'object' | 'description' | null`, which checks in that field order: for `NOTE` the slug, the type, the body (required, at least one non-whitespace character, at most 8192 UTF-8 bytes), then the description (required, 1..200 chars after trim); for any other kind only that `description` is absent. The REST write path and the assistant tool both call it. A note's active key is `NOTE:<slug>`, so re-saving a slug with a new type, body or description supersedes the old note; an identical restatement (same type, body, description, source) is the existing no-op.

**Scope** — In: MemoryKind.NOTE, nullable description column and domain/DTO mappings, shared validation, REST service validation and active-key lookups in upsert/findActive. Add migration 20261121090000_memory_note_description. Preserve transaction-local replacement checks/audit and all triple behavior. Update existing query-shape and fixture assertions, endpoint e2e and regenerate OpenAPI/client using bun run generate. Out: assistant registration/rendering (US-002), full-text search (US-003), user scope (US-004/005), export (US-006), note retire (US-011). No pending memory rows and no `status: pending` value: proposal mode is a project approval policy on `memory.create` for AGENT principals (ruling 2026-11-03); an unapproved write simply does not exist yet.

**Interface** — `MemoryKind` gains `NOTE: 'NOTE'`. `MemoryItem` and `MemoryItemInput` gain `description?: string`; `CreateMemoryDto` adds `description?: string` (string, max 200). `buildActiveKey(_projectId, kind, subject, predicate)` answers `NOTE:<subject>` when `kind` is `NOTE`; unchanged for every other kind. `PrismaMemoryItemRepository.upsert(item: MemoryItemInput, options?)` finds the active project row by `{ projectId, activeKey, deletedAt: null }`; its no-op also compares `predicate` and `description`. `PrismaMemoryItemRepository.findActive(projectId, kind, subject, predicate)` matches `{ projectId, activeKey: buildActiveKey(projectId, kind, subject, predicate), status: 'active', deletedAt: null }`. `noteFieldError(input: { kind: string; subject: string; predicate: string; object?: string; description?: string }): 'subject' | 'predicate' | 'object' | 'description' | null`. A validation failure throws ValidationAppException naming the field in the memory domain before persistence.

Verification: co-located pure validation tests plus real-Postgres write/supersession/no-op tests and REST 201/400 checks; preserve current decision-create refusal and permission checks.

userStories.title: Write, list and fetch notes through assistant and MCP tools
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Expose NOTE writes and safe two-stage note recall through the assistant registry and derived MCP catalog.

A note-shaped item: MemoryItem is a subject/predicate/object triple in the kinds FACT, DECISION, PREFERENCE, CONSTRAINT and INCIDENT_PATTERN; nax needs to write, list and fetch Markdown notes through the assistant and MCP tools (#376).

**Approach** — `koda_add_memory` accepts `NOTE` with `description`, through the same `noteFieldError`; for a NOTE the tool's 4000-character `object` cap does not apply (the 8192-byte note cap does). `koda_get_memory` reads through a new `MemoryGovernanceService.getMemoryItem(projectId, id, owner?)`, which loads the row with the repository's `findById` and answers it only when it is not soft-deleted and is either a row of `projectId` or (after US-005) a user row whose `ownerKey` is the owner's; otherwise null. `KnowledgeTools`' constructor is unchanged (it already holds `MemoryGovernanceService`). `koda_memory_search` lists a note as its header line plus one fenced line `<slug> <type> <description>`, never the body. A new `koda_get_memory` (`getMemoryTool` in `tools/knowledge-tools.ts`, `memory.read`, read kind) takes `{ id }` and answers the header line, the fenced description (notes only) and the fenced body. After US-005 the header line of every listed or fetched item ends with `scope project` or `scope user`.

**Scope** — In: add-memory parse/preview/execute carries description and reuses US-001's validator; NOTE descriptor/schema limits; getMemoryItem project/deletion checks; getMemoryTool parse, body rendering and registry registration; MCP projection and tool-name pins. Update REPO/PROJECT/WORKSPACE counts from 22/22/23 to 23/23/24 and the existing assistant-design tool table. Preserve FACT fenced triples and replace authorization during preview and execute. Out: scope-aware caller reads/header tags belong to US-005; full-text ordering belongs to US-003. No MCP twin of the export route (`koda_memory_export`); HTTP is the only export surface. US-011 only: no CLI command and no assistant or MCP tool retires a note; nax calls the REST route.

**Interface** — `MemoryGovernanceService.getMemoryItem(projectId, id, owner?)`; `getMemoryTool` in `tools/knowledge-tools.ts`; `AddMemoryInput` gains `description?`; `KODA_ADD_MEMORY` / `MEMORY_WRITE_KINDS` gain NOTE and description (max 200); `KNOWLEDGE_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS` gains `KODA_GET_MEMORY`. `KODA_GET_MEMORY` requires id (1-64 chars), additionalProperties false, key memory.read. `noteFieldError(input: { kind: string; subject: string; predicate: string; object?: string; description?: string }): 'subject' | 'predicate' | 'object' | 'description' | null` is the only note validator. `parse` reports ToolInputError naming the field. NOTE preview starts `Remember in <slug>: NOTE replay-budget / project`, includes description and ends with the active replacement id when one exists, even if type changed. execute passes description to upsert and returns `memory:<id> saved`. Missing/foreign/deleted fetches answer `memory item not found`, not an error.

Verification: co-located parser/preview/rendering/catalog/registry tests plus getMemoryItem DB isolation and a registered MCP call exercising AssistantToolExecutor.executeFor with origin mcp. Keep all untrusted memory text inside ctx.data fences.

userStories.title: Rank memory recall with PostgreSQL full-text search
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Replace substring-only memory recall with ranked PostgreSQL full-text search while preserving existing fallback and eligibility semantics.

**Motivation** — Stemmed and multi-word queries miss, and nothing is ranked (#377).

**Approach** — The migration adds `"searchVector" tsvector GENERATED ALWAYS AS (to_tsvector('english', coalesce("subject", '') || ' ' || coalesce("predicate", '') || ' ' || coalesce("description", '') || ' ' || coalesce("object", ''))) STORED` and a GIN index on it. The migration SQL is hand-written; the schema declares the column as `Unsupported("tsvector")?` so Prisma does not try to drop it. Tests build their schema with `prisma db push --force-reset` (`test/global-setup.ts`), which would create a plain, never-filled `tsvector`; a new `test/helpers/memory-search-vector.ts` exports `MEMORY_SEARCH_VECTOR_STATEMENTS` (drop the pushed column, add the generated column, create the GIN index), `global-setup.ts` replays them after the push next to `PARTIAL_UNIQUE_INDEXES`, and a unit spec pins that every statement except the drop is shipped verbatim by the migration. Hand-written index names equal Prisma's defaults: `MemoryItem_searchVector_idx`, `MemoryItem_ownerKey_activeKey_key`, `MemoryItem_projectId_updatedAt_id_idx`, `MemoryItem_ownerKey_updatedAt_id_idx`. When `ProjectMemoryQuery.text` is non-blank, the repository first asks Postgres whether `websearch_to_tsquery('english', text)` has any lexeme (`numnode(...) > 0`). With lexemes, one `$queryRaw` (tagged template, every value bound) selects the page of ids with every other filter applied in SQL (project or owner, `deletedAt IS NULL`, status, the TTL bound when status is defaulted, kind, subject prefix), ordered by `ts_rank("searchVector", query) DESC, "updatedAt" DESC, "id" DESC` when `orderBy` is absent and by the requested `orderBy` (with its existing tiebreakers) otherwise, with `OFFSET`/`LIMIT` from the page; a second `$queryRaw` counts the matches; the rows are then loaded with Prisma by id and returned in the ranked order. The subject prefix in SQL is `starts_with("subject", ${prefix})`, so `%` and `_` are literal. Without lexemes (stopwords only, punctuation) the existing `contains` path runs unchanged; when the full-text count is 0 the `contains` path also runs, so a Chinese (or other unsegmented) query that the `english` parser cannot split still finds the substring matches it found before this feature. The text term is always an `AND` with the TTL bound (S5b US-004 invariant).

**Scope** — In: generated column/Gin migration 20261121090100_memory_full_text_search, schema declaration, trusted test schema replay helper, ranked repository path and count/hydration, ListMemoryQuery.text (1-100 chars), assistant default rank ordering for text and descriptor wording. The owner-aware extension is supplied in US-005; at this dependency stage keep project filters intact. Out: scope storage/reads (US-004/005), export indexes (US-006), UI search controls (US-008), CLI commands (US-010); No hybrid vector plus keyword ranking; the knowledge base (LanceDB) stays the semantic layer. Full-text search uses the `english` configuration only; no Chinese segmentation is added (unsegmented text falls back to the substring match).

**Interface** — `ProjectMemoryQuery` remains `{ projectId, kind?, subject?, text?, status?, orderBy? }` in this story; `orderBy` absent with a text that has lexemes means rank order. `ListMemoryQuery` adds `text?: string` (1-100 chars). `PrismaMemoryItemRepository.findByProjectMemory(query: ProjectMemoryQuery, page: IPageOption): Promise<IPageResult<MemoryItem>>`. `MEMORY_SEARCH_VECTOR_STATEMENTS` is exported by `apps/api/test/helpers/memory-search-vector.ts`. `memorySearchTool.execute` passes no orderBy when text is set and 'updatedAt' otherwise. Prisma gains `searchVector Unsupported("tsvector")?` and `@@index([searchVector], type: Gin)`.

Verification: real Postgres tests for stemming, ranking, filters, TTL, literal prefixes, stable pagination, injection-shaped text and Chinese/no-lexeme fallback; DTO/unit ordering tests; trusted SQL migration parity unit test co-located at src/memory/memory-search-vector.spec.ts per repository instructions. Update both repository mock suites to stub the lexeme probe on fallback tests, global-setup replay assertions, endpoint e2e and regenerated contract.

userStories.title: Write principal-owned user-scoped notes
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Store NOTE memory once per calling principal across projects while retaining project-gated write authorization and approval.

**Motivation** — Every item needs a projectId; user-level working agreements cannot be stored once and recalled in every project (#378).

**Approach** — `scope: 'user'` is accepted only for `kind: 'NOTE'`. The request still names a `projectId`: membership, `memory.create` and the approval policy are all checked against it exactly as for a project write, so a project in proposal mode also holds a user note for approval. The stored row has `projectId: null`, `scope: 'user'`, `ownerType`/`ownerId` = the caller (an `ownerId` in the body is ignored for user scope, even for a global admin), and `ownerKey` = `${ownerType}:${ownerId}`. `ownerKey` is set only on user rows, so `@@unique([ownerKey, activeKey])` keys a principal's user notes and never touches project rows (null `ownerKey` is distinct in Postgres); `@@unique([projectId, activeKey])` keeps keying project rows (user rows have null `projectId`). Reads that pass `owner` include the owner's user rows next to the project's rows: `GET /projects/:slug/memory`, the export, `koda_memory_search` and `koda_get_memory`. Reads that do not pass `owner` (the context builder, governance, canonical state, review decisions) never see user rows, because every one of them filters on a `projectId`.

**Scope** — In: write side of that design only: MemoryScope, nullable persisted/domain projectId, scope/ownerKey mapping and user active-key lookup, caller-only ownership, same-project gate/audit context and decision-retire user-row exclusion. Migration 20261121090200_memory_user_scope keeps the project active-key unique and adds the owner active-key unique. Mechanical type fixture fixes must not broaden any background read. Out: including user rows in REST/tools (US-005), export (US-006) and the new note-retire route (US-011). No org-wide memory, and no Agent-to-User ownership: a user-scoped item is owned by the principal that wrote it. User scope is NOTE-only; triples (FACT, DECISION, PREFERENCE, CONSTRAINT, INCIDENT_PATTERN) stay project-scoped.

**Interface** — `MemoryScope = { PROJECT: 'project', USER: 'user' }` and its type in common/enums. `MemoryItem` / `MemoryItemInput`: `projectId: string | null` (null exactly for a user item), `description?: string`, `scope: MemoryScope` on the domain, `scope?` on the input, `ownerKey?: string` on the domain; the repository derives ownerKey as `${ownerType}:${ownerId}` when scope is user. `CreateMemoryDto` adds `scope?: 'project' | 'user'`; its request projectId remains required. `PrismaMemoryItemRepository.upsert(item: MemoryItemInput, options?)` finds the active project row by `{ projectId, activeKey }`, or user row by `{ ownerKey, activeKey }`, with `deletedAt: null`. `memoryAuditHook(audit, key, projectId?: string)` records `written.item.projectId ?? projectId`. `MemoryWriteService.retireTarget` still returns `{ projectId: string }`; `assertRetireTarget` answers `NotFoundAppException({}, 'memory.notFound')` for scope user before membership. Prisma: `projectId String?`, `project Project?` (still onDelete Cascade), `scope String @default("project")`, `ownerKey String?`, `@@unique([ownerKey, activeKey])` named MemoryItem_ownerKey_activeKey_key.

Verification: real-Postgres REST ownership, cross-project supersession/isolation and approval-as-requester tests; audit fallback test; regress project writes and old retire semantics; regenerate contract and Prisma client.

userStories.title: Recall caller-owned user notes alongside project memory
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Include only the caller's user notes in project memory lists and assistant single-item/list recall, with scope filtering and scope-tagged tool headers.

**Motivation** — Every item needs a projectId; user-level working agreements cannot be stored once and recalled in every project (#378).

**Approach** — `scope: 'user'` is accepted only for `kind: 'NOTE'`. The request still names a `projectId`: membership, `memory.create` and the approval policy are all checked against it exactly as for a project write, so a project in proposal mode also holds a user note for approval. The stored row has `projectId: null`, `scope: 'user'`, `ownerType`/`ownerId` = the caller (an `ownerId` in the body is ignored for user scope, even for a global admin), and `ownerKey` = `${ownerType}:${ownerId}`. `ownerKey` is set only on user rows, so `@@unique([ownerKey, activeKey])` keys a principal's user notes and never touches project rows (null `ownerKey` is distinct in Postgres); `@@unique([projectId, activeKey])` keeps keying project rows (user rows have null `projectId`). Reads that pass `owner` include the owner's user rows next to the project's rows: `GET /projects/:slug/memory`, the export, `koda_memory_search` and `koda_get_memory`. Reads that do not pass `owner` (the context builder, governance, canonical state, review decisions) never see user rows, because every one of them filters on a `projectId`.

Assistant read design: `koda_get_memory` reads through a new `MemoryGovernanceService.getMemoryItem(projectId, id, owner?)`, which loads the row with the repository's `findById` and answers it only when it is not soft-deleted and is either a row of `projectId` or (after US-005) a user row whose `ownerKey` is the owner's; otherwise null. `KnowledgeTools`' constructor is unchanged (it already holds `MemoryGovernanceService`). After US-005 the header line of every listed or fetched item ends with `scope project` or `scope user`.

**Scope** — In: owner/scope query contract; identical authorized union in substring and full-text paths; Principal in getMemory; ctx.actor in memorySearchTool/getMemoryTool; getMemoryItem owner isolation and trailing tool scope tags. Out: storage and write attribution (US-004), export route (US-006), tool introduction/registration (US-002), UI (US-008); `MemoryGovernanceService` (expire, downrank, dedupe, supersession), extraction, canonical state, review decisions and the `/context` builder are unchanged and never read user-scoped rows. A user note written through project Q is visible to its owner in every project, including a proposal-mode project P that never held it for approval; per-project review of user notes is not added. userStories.title: Export incremental memory changes including tombstones
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Give nax an authorized incremental HTTP feed over project and caller-owned user memory changes.

**Motivation** — The only keyset read is findActiveAfterId, by id and active rows only, so supersede, retire and soft delete of old rows are invisible to a mirror (#379).

**Approach** — `GET /projects/:slug/memory/export?since=<cursor>&take=<n>`, `memory.read`, guarded like the list. It returns every row of the project plus the caller's user rows with `(updatedAt, id)` strictly after the cursor, ordered `updatedAt ASC, id ASC`, every status and kind, soft-deleted rows included (they carry `deletedAt`). A row supersede, retire or soft delete goes through Prisma `update`, which bumps `updatedAt`, so the change reappears after the cursor. Rows whose `updatedAt` is within `MEMORY_EXPORT_SETTLE_MS = 5000` of the server clock are held back to the next call, so a transaction that commits late with an earlier `updatedAt` is not skipped. The cursor is `encodeMemoryExportCursor({ updatedAt, id })` / `decodeMemoryExportCursor(cursor): MemoryExportKey | null` in a new `apps/api/src/memory/memory-export-cursor.ts`, the same base64url `iso|id` shape as `timeline-cursor.ts`. `take` defaults to 100, range 1..500. The response is `JsonResponse.Ok({ items: MemoryItem[], nextCursor: string | null, hasMore: boolean })`: `nextCursor` is the cursor of the last item, or the `since` given when the page is empty (null when neither exists); `hasMore` is true exactly when `items.length === take`. Rows are returned as stored; fencing is an LLM-prompt concern and stays in the MCP tools.

**Scope** — In: strict cursor codec, ExportMemoryQuery, repository changed-row keyset read, governance settle-window composition, memory.read-guarded export route and indexes migration 20261121090300_memory_export_indexes. Include all statuses/TTL/deleted rows without normal list eligibility filters; authorization is still the project/caller union. Out: list owner/scope filtering (US-005), write-mode (US-007), creating the note-retire operation (US-011), or an event-history table. No MCP twin of the export route (`koda_memory_export`); HTTP is the only export surface. Export and list responses are not fenced; fencing stays in the MCP tool text.

**Interface** — `encodeMemoryExportCursor({ updatedAt, id })`; `decodeMemoryExportCursor(cursor): MemoryExportKey | null`. `findChangedAfter(scope: { projectId: string; ownerKey: string }, after: MemoryExportKey | null, until: Date, take: number): Promise<MemoryItem[]>`. `MemoryGovernanceService.exportProjectMemory(projectId, owner, since, take)` composes the cursor, settle window and page. `ExportMemoryQuery` supplies since and take (integer 1..500, default 100). Prisma adds `@@index([projectId, updatedAt, id])` and `@@index([ownerKey, updatedAt, id])`, with names MemoryItem_projectId_updatedAt_id_idx and MemoryItem_ownerKey_updatedAt_id_idx. Use @Principal to derive owner, ProjectMembershipGuard then RequiresGuard and @Requires('memory.read'), and ProjectAccessService slug resolution.

Verification: pure cursor/DTO/fake-clock tests; real-Postgres same-timestamp pagination, re-export of changed rows, tombstones, settle exclusion and ownership isolation; REST invalid query/permission/project cases. Use controlled updatedAt/clock fixtures rather than sleeps; regenerate OpenAPI.

userStories.title: Resolve the caller's effective memory write mode
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Report the approval gate's effective memory.create mode and the project's exact editable AGENT policy through a read-only route.

**Codebase mapping** — KodaPrincipal exposes actorType ('user' | 'agent' | 'runner'), and ToolContext.actor is restricted to user/agent principals; neither supplies the uppercase approval subject type assumed by the spec's principal.type notation. Existing route guards exclude runners. For an authorized user/agent caller, derive the resolver subject with the existing ownerTypeFor(principal): subject: { type: ownerTypeFor(principal), id: principal.id }. The spec expressions below describe that normalized subject, not a new field on KodaPrincipal. Do not use a cast or change the principal interface to invent principal.type.

**Motivation** — A project that wants agent memory writes reviewed first has no setting for it (#380).

**Approach** — `GET /projects/:slug/memory/write-mode`, `memory.read`, answers `{ mode: 'direct' | 'proposal', policyId: string | null, source: 'policy' | 'default' | 'not-approvable', agentPolicy: { id: string; mode: ApprovalMode } | null }`. `MemoryWriteModeService.resolve(projectId, principal)` answers the mode the gate would apply to the CALLER's own `memory.create` write: it calls `ApprovalPolicyResolver.resolve({ key: 'memory.create', projectId, subject: { type: principal.type, id: principal.id } })` (the engine's own ranking: project before global, principal before role before type before all, wildcard patterns included). For an AGENT caller `mode` is `proposal` when the resolved mode is not `none`; for a USER caller `mode` is always `direct`, because `ApprovalGate.gate` executes a USER's write directly. `policyId` and `source` come from the resolver's answer. `agentPolicy` is the project's exact type-AGENT policy (`permissionPattern` `memory.create`, `principalType` `AGENT`, no role, no principal), read with `ApprovalPolicyService.list({ projectId, permissionPattern: 'memory.create' }, ...)`, or null; it is what the web toggle edits. Writing the mode is the existing policy routes. The web toggle (US-009) shows proposal when `agentPolicy` exists with a mode other than `none`; choosing proposal creates `{ permissionPattern: 'memory.create', appliesTo: { kind: 'type', principalType: 'AGENT' }, mode: 'human' }` when `agentPolicy` is null, or patches it to `mode: 'human'` when it exists in mode `none` (a second create would collide on the selector); choosing direct deletes it.

**Scope** — In: MemoryWriteModeService and its resolver/policy collaborators, module provider registration, memory.read-guarded GET write-mode, response documentation/contract. Reuse existing ApprovalEngineModule exports; do not add a second approval engine. Out: web mutation control (US-009), note storage/scope/export and note retire (US-001/004/006/011); No project column for the write mode; the mode is derived from approval policies on every read. No pending memory rows and no `status: pending` value: proposal mode is a project approval policy on `memory.create` for AGENT principals (ruling 2026-11-03); an unapproved write simply does not exist yet.

**Interface** — `MemoryWriteModeService.resolve(projectId, principal)`; for the raw KodaPrincipal implementation, `ApprovalPolicyResolver.resolve({ key: 'memory.create', projectId, subject: { type: ownerTypeFor(principal), id: principal.id } })`; `ApprovalPolicyService.list(filter: { projectId?: string | null; permissionPattern?: string }, page: { current: number; size: number }): Promise<ApprovalPolicyRecord[]>`. GET returns `JsonResponse.Ok({ mode, policyId, source, agentPolicy })`. Provide MemoryWriteModeService in MemoryModule and inject it into MemoryReadController, updating constructor doubles.

Verification: pure resolver/mapping/selector unit tests and DB-free module DI tests; real guarded-route policy/default and actual POST gate-consistency checks. Regenerate OpenAPI for the new route and retain current read status codes.

**Goal** — Extend the thin memory CLI with NOTE description/scope input and paged list/full-text search commands using the generated client.

Memory create, list and search need CLI surfaces for notes (#376), full-text search (#377) and user scope (#378).

**Approach** — Regenerated client; `memory create` takes `--description` and `--scope`; new `memory list` and `memory search <text>`. `create` gains `--description` and `--scope` and lists NOTE in `--kind`, and validates option values before resolving the project; adds `list` and `search`.

**Scope** — In: memory.ts options, early enum/paging validation, generated read/write SDK use, pretty JSON page output, concise human records, stderr/exit semantics and command tests. Run bun run generate:cli from the updated committed OpenAPI (or bun run generate to refresh both); never hand-edit generated types/sdk/index. Out: web UI, export CLI and reimplementing note body/domain rules in the CLI (option syntax, enum and paging checks above remain in scope). Existing memory retire remains decision-only. US-011 only: no CLI command and no assistant or MCP tool retires a note; nax calls the REST route.

**Interface** — `koda memory create --project alpha --kind NOTE --subject replay-budget --predicate project --object "body" --description "replay budget" [--scope project|user]`. `koda memory list --project alpha [--kind NOTE] [--scope project|user|all] [--page <n>] [--json]` calls GET /projects/alpha/memory with kind/scope and the corresponding current page. `koda memory search <text> --project alpha` calls the same generated read operation with text. For --json print the entire unwrapped page as `JSON.stringify(data, null, 2)`; without it print one line per record containing id, kind, scope and NOTE description or non-NOTE subject predicate. API or network errors go to stderr with exit 1; invalid option values go to stderr with exit 3 and no API call. Validate before resolving the project. create carries description/scope in the generated create DTO.

Verification: Jest generated-client mocks and Commander parseAsync cases for request arguments, output formatting, option failure before project lookup, API/network error exit 1 (500) and invalid-page/scope exit 3. Use the shared handleApiError unchanged (401/403 stay exit 2); preserve decision retire and approval-pending behavior outside this story's specified failure cases.

[cli] koda memory list --project alpha without --json prints one line per record with id, kind, scope and the description for a NOTE or subject predicate otherwise.
[cli] koda memory search "deployed runner" --project alpha calls GET /projects/alpha/memory with text=deployed runner and exits 0.

[cli] When a memory create, list or search API call fails with an API or network error, the command prints the error to stderr and exits 1.
[cli] When memory create writes a FACT without --description or --scope, it forwards the existing subject, predicate and object options unchanged to memoryControllerCreateMemory and exits 0.

acceptanceCriteria: [integration] POST /memory/notes/:id/retire by the agent that owns an active project NOTE answers 201, and the row is rejected with a null activeKey.

[integration] After that retire, with the system clock advanced past MEMORY_EXPORT_SETTLE_MS (updatedAt is set client-side, so a faked clock moves it), an export with the cursor taken before the retire returns the row with status 'rejected'.
[integration] After that retire, POST /memory of a NOTE with the same slug in the same project stores a new active row.
[integration] POST /memory/notes/:id/retire for a FACT id answers 422 and leaves the row active.
[integration] POST /memory/notes/:id/retire for a superseded NOTE answers 409 memory.retireNotActive.
[integration] For an unknown id, a soft-deleted NOTE, or a NOTE of a project the caller is not a member of, the route answers 404 memory.notFound.
[integration] Agent B, a project member without an any-row memory.update grant, retiring agent A's project NOTE answers 403 and leaves the row active.
[integration] Agent A retiring its own user NOTE with { projectId: P }, P a project A is a member of, answers 201 and the row is rejected.
[integration] Agent B retiring agent A's user NOTE with { projectId: P } answers 404 and leaves the row active.
[integration] Agent A retiring its own user NOTE without projectId in the body answers 400 naming projectId, and with a projectId A is not a member of answers 404.
[integration] In a project P whose memory.create AGENT policy is human, an agent's retire of a FACT id answers 422 and opens no approval request.

[integration] With a project P policy memory.create for type AGENT in mode human, agent A's retire of its project NOTE answers 202 with a pending approval request and the row stays active; after a user approves it through POST /approvals/:id/decisions, the row is rejected.
[integration] A retire with reason: 'stale' records one audit entry with key memory.create, the row's id and summary retired NOTE: stale.
[unit] RetireNoteDto with a 501-character reason fails validation on reason.
[integration] In a proposal-mode project, retiring an inactive NOTE answers 409 memory.retireNotActive before the gate and opens no approval request.
[integration] When MemoryWriteGuard.mayReplace refuses retirement of another principal's project NOTE, the route answers 403 permissions.
[integration] Given an active project DECISION and an authorized owner with memory.decision.retire, POST /memory/:id/retire still answers 201 and leaves that decision rejected with a null activeKey.
[integration] Given a project NOTE and an authorized project member, POST /memory/:id/retire still answers 422 rather than retiring it, preserving the old route's decision-only contract.

routing.reasoning: The new route reuses existing decision-retire row locking, audit callbacks and approval-command variants, with additional ordered user-note checks; authorization and locked revalidation require strict security TDD.

analysis:
Existing-system enhancement closing #376, #377, #378, #379 and #380; not greenfield. Navigation used direct reads and text search because this host exposes no codebase-memory MCP tools. The execution root is /Users/williamkhoo/workspace/subrina-coder/projects/koda/repos/koda. Read the package contexts before implementation. The supplied automatic stack labels Express and Next.js are inaccurate: the repository guidance identifies NestJS 12/Fastify/Prisma 7 for API and Nuxt 4/Vue for web (.nax/mono/apps/api/context.md:22; .nax/mono/apps/web/context.md:23). Bun workspaces and Turbo orchestrate the packages (package.json:5). Implementation agents must read the nathapp-nestjs-patterns skill before writing NestJS; it was not present under that name in repository files in this session. Keep Nathapp exceptions, JsonResponse envelopes, repository/transaction-manager patterns and generated Prisma imports. This PRD writes planning JSON only, not application code.

Current persistence and write seams: MemoryItem is a string-kind triple with mandatory projectId, optional object/owner/source, activeKey, soft delete and Prisma-managed updatedAt; only (projectId, activeKey) is unique (apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma:648). Domain inputs and output types currently have no description/scope/ownerKey, and projectId is non-null (apps/api/src/memory/memory-item-repository.ts:16). buildActiveKey currently always includes predicate (apps/api/src/memory/prisma-memory-item.repository.ts:17). upsert is serializable, executes beforeSupersede and onWritten inside its transaction, and intentionally performs no mutation/audit for an identical restatement (same file:199). Its old lookup matches kind/subject/predicate rather than activeKey; both this and findActive must use NOTE:<slug>, otherwise changing a note type evades replacement checks or collides on uniqueness. Map description in all persistence/domain directions and include predicate and description in no-op comparison, normalizing optional values consistently with stored nulls. Preserve other kinds' keys and no-op semantics. MemoryWriteService.create checks project membership and memory.create, refuses generic DECISION creation, and permits attributed ownership only with global memory.update (apps/api/src/memory/memory-write.service.ts:44, 226). User-note ownership must override that attribution path even for administrators. Keep the request project as the authorization/approval/audit context while storing null projectId for user notes. MemoryWriteGuard passes a typed createdBy resource into memory.update and is used by REST, extraction and assistant writes (apps/api/src/memory/memory-write.guard.ts:49). memoryAuditHook currently copies item.projectId directly and must accept a fallback gate project for user items (apps/api/src/memory/memory-audit.ts:33).

Reads and search: MemoryReadController already has the right project membership then RequiresGuard order and memory.read permission, resolves slug through ProjectAccessService and parses Koda paging before returning the standard page (apps/api/src/memory/memory-read.controller.ts:24). It currently has no Principal parameter. MemoryGovernanceService.getProjectMemory delegates to the repository; cleanup explicitly supplies projectId through findActiveAfterId/findByProject (apps/api/src/memory/memory-governance.service.ts:26, 47). findByProjectMemory uses active + TTL by default, literal subject prefix through Prisma, an AND-contained ILIKE OR over subject/predicate/object, and stable confidence/updatedAt/createdAt/id ordering (apps/api/src/memory/prisma-memory-item.repository.ts:368). Keep the TTL AND invariant in BOTH SQL and fallback paths. Full-text rank applies only for non-blank text with lexemes and no explicit orderBy; preserve explicit-order tiebreakers and fallback substring behavior, including no-lexeme and zero-full-text-match fallback for unsegmented text. Never fall back merely because an offset page is empty when total is nonzero. Bind all raw SQL values with tagged templates; whitelist sort fragments and use starts_with for literal %/_ prefixes. The raw id query and count must share authorization, scope, soft-delete, status, kind, prefix and TTL filters; hydrate by id and restore SQL order. Scope defaults to all only when owner is supplied; without owner a read remains project-only, and scope=user yields no rows. Group project-or-owner predicates separately from text and TTL so an OR cannot leak another principal's user notes.

Affected dependents: the domain types are imported by extraction, the outbox subscriber, governance, audit, context, review decisions, assistant tools and many fixtures. Update type fixtures with project scope without broadening these consumers' behavior. ContextBuilderService calls findByProjectMemory with only projectId and confidence ordering, so it must remain project-only (apps/api/src/context/context-builder.service.ts:110). Canonical state, review decisions, cleanup, extraction and /context must never receive owner. findReviewDecisionRows also explicitly filters projectId (apps/api/src/memory/prisma-memory-item.repository.ts:341). Nullable projectId requires defensive narrowing in decision retirement rather than a non-null assertion that could authorize a user row. Existing assertRetireTarget masks only membership ForbiddenAppException as notFound, not infrastructure errors (apps/api/src/memory/memory-write.service.ts:190). Preserve that distinction.

Assistant/MCP seams: addMemoryTool parses fields by hand, masks preview text, checks replacement during preview, and writes with a transaction-local guard/audit hook (apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/tools/add-memory-tool.ts:66). Its current 4000-character cap must remain for triples but not notes, whose limit is 8192 UTF-8 bytes. Its catalog schema currently also caps object globally at MAX_BODY_CHARS, so expose note-compatible schema/wording rather than letting schema validation reject valid notes (apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/koda-tool-descriptors.ts:461). knowledge-tools.ts already holds MemoryGovernanceService in an unchanged KnowledgeTools constructor; memorySearchTool currently orders newest and fences each triple through ctx.data (apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/tools/knowledge-tools.ts:125, 230). Register getMemoryTool there, give it memory.read, and fence note description/body with the same data mechanism. List notes by description, never body. The catalog is projected into MCP, with descriptions rewritten and koda_list_approvals deliberately filtered out; preserve that projection rather than adding bespoke MCP endpoints (apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/mcp/mcp-tool-catalog.ts:93). Update descriptor/catalog/module/tool-name pins and the spec's counts from 22/22/23 to 23/23/24 if still current. Read tools include the ctx.actor owner after US-005; the add tool's new scope input is NOT requested. The existing assistant/MCP execution gate continues governing memory.create.

Approval seams: createMemory already uses @ApprovalGated with memory.create and variant rest:memory.create; pending means ApprovalPending/202, not a MemoryItem (apps/api/src/memory/memory.controller.ts:74). MemoryRouteCommands parses DTOs and executes under the requester loaded by ActorPrincipalLoader (apps/api/src/memory/memory-route.commands.ts:38). ApprovalGate resolves policies, directly executes USER subjects regardless of resolved mode, and opens pending requests for other callers when mode is not none (apps/api/src/approvals/approval-gate.service.ts:108). ApprovalPolicyResolver already owns project-before-global and principal/role/type/all ranking, wildcard specificity and mode floors (apps/api/src/approvals/approval-policy.resolver.ts:30). Reuse it, do not reproduce ranking. ApprovalPolicyService.list returns one page's records, not an unbounded list (apps/api/src/approvals/approval-policy.service.ts:98); when finding the exact project AGENT policy, do not confuse an inherited/global, role or principal policy with the editable selector, or miss it on a later page. Existing project policy POST/PATCH/DELETE are all approval.policy.manage guarded and selector identity is immutable (apps/api/src/approvals/project-approval-policies.controller.ts:69, 94, 117). A policy in mode none must be patched to human, not created again. The settings control edits agentPolicy, not the USER caller's always-direct mode; deleting the exact policy does not promise the effective AGENT mode is direct if inherited/wildcard policies still resolve to proposal.

Export and retirement: copy the timeline cursor's base64url ISO|id conventions but key by updatedAt ascending, with strict validation and a unique id tiebreaker (apps/api/src/memory/timeline-cursor.ts:10). Export is a bounded current-row change feed, not an append-only event history or an active-item list. Include all statuses, expired rows and soft-delete tombstones; exclude only unrelated project/owner rows and rows inside the 5000ms settle window. Return the input cursor unchanged on empty pages and set hasMore exactly to length===take, not based on an extra-row probe. Prisma update already bumps updatedAt for supersede/reject/softDelete/retire (apps/api/src/memory/prisma-memory-item.repository.ts:234, 301, 319); do not bypass these updates. The settle window mitigates late commits but is not a claim of arbitrary-transaction-duration losslessness. Note retirement reuses the existing row-lock retire transaction, callbacks and rejected/null-activeKey mutation (same file:301). Validate the ordered preflight before opening approval, then repeat target/ownership/kind/active and replacement checks under lock. Gate under memory.create with rest:memory.note.retire; leave the old decision-only route and permission untouched. Audit remains inside the mutation transaction with gate-project fallback for user notes, and i18n keys/exceptions remain the same with broader decision-and-note messages.

Web: the memory page currently has only ['', FACT, INCIDENT_PATTERN, DECISION] and always interpolates object (apps/web/pages/[project]/memory.vue:23, 109). Add all six kinds in the exact requested order, a description-first NOTE row with an expandable body, a user-only badge and 300ms trailing text debounce. Continue interpolation for agent-written Markdown, not v-html. useMemory owns the paging/filter state, request-id stale-response suppression, append failure rollback and structured records (apps/web/composables/useMemory.ts:29, 46); preserve those semantics and reset paging on search changes. New UI copy belongs in both locale JSONs. Settings has four existing tabs and extracted cards (apps/web/pages/[project]/settings.vue:77); add SettingsMemoryCard with the slug without rearranging navigation. SettingsKnowledgeCard is the permission-gated loading/retry/error pattern (apps/web/components/SettingsKnowledgeCard.vue:34). useApprovalPolicies already exposes create/update/remove and project-root helpers (apps/web/composables/useApprovalPolicies.ts:75); use it for policy mutation and the new useMemoryWriteMode for the read snapshot. Follow extractApiError, prevent writes without approval.policy.manage, disable pending controls, and restore the last reported selection on failure. UX redesign guidance requires preserving tokens/layout pins and updating the MASTER-PLAN status/decisions when changing layout (docs/ux/redesign/MASTER-PLAN.md:33); do not turn this feature into a navigation redesign.

CLI: memoryCommand already registers retire (decisions only), timeline, decisions and create; write commands resolve project slug to id and use generated operations, unwrap and handleApiError (apps/cli/src/commands/memory.ts:13, 133). Add description/scope plus list/search using the regenerated read operation. Validate options BEFORE project resolution/network access, map --page to API current, preserve JSON page metadata and print one human line per item. Important incompatibility: shared handleApiError currently maps 403/auth to exit 2 and 404 to 4, while this spec requires API/network failures for the new memory surface to exit 1 and invalid option values to exit 3 (apps/cli/src/utils/error.ts:96). Implement narrowly scoped handling or an opt-in helper behavior, not a repository-wide error semantic change; preserve existing decision retire/timeline/approval-pending behavior outside the specified commands. The generated SDK is the only networking boundary; do not add handwritten endpoint wiring.

Migration sequence and rollout: US-001 adds nullable description; US-003 adds generated english tsvector/Gin; US-004 makes projectId and relation nullable, adds scope default project and ownerKey unique; US-006 adds the two change-feed composite indexes. Keep the existing project active-key unique constraint. Use the exact migration directory names and Prisma-default index names in the story descriptions. Existing rows backfill as project scope with null ownerKey and unchanged triple keys. Deploy compatible schema before code relying on fields; regenerate the Prisma client after schema edits. The generated search column derives from subject, predicate, description and object. prisma db push cannot build its expression: replay trusted MEMORY_SEARCH_VECTOR_STATEMENTS after partial indexes in test/global-setup.ts, and pin all statements except the test-only drop to migration SQL verbatim. Do not let a later Prisma migration replace the generated column with a plain tsvector or rename hand-written indexes. Shared Prisma fixture types may require mechanical updates across packages. The full-text parity unit spec is planned at src/memory/memory-search-vector.spec.ts instead of the spec's proposed test/unit/memory path, to obey the repository's co-located unit-test instruction; its helper and integration filenames remain as specified.

OpenAPI/client rollout: package.json:21 defines bun run generate as API build/export then generate:cli; all REST DTO/controller stories regenerate openapi.json and CLI outputs rather than editing generated code. The binding workdirs remain apps/api, apps/web and apps/cli exactly as requested, with root OpenAPI/downstream generated artifacts as the documented contract-generation exception. In particular US-005 enhances methods introduced by US-002 but its mandated dependencies do not include US-002; integration must coordinate these shared-file changes and retain both the getMemoryTool implementation and owner extension, without silently adding a dependency or moving ACs. Both repository unit suites with substring mocks need the lexeme probe stub, not only the additional spec. Keep every existing behavior assertion meaningful while updating changed query-shape pins. Existing DB suites include permissions-memory-routes, gated-memory-routes, memory-upsert-replay, memory-governance-paging and assistant-add-memory-tool; new specs extend these patterns. Update endpoint e2e cases per story (NOTE happy/invalid, text limit, user-scope kind restrictions, scope filter validation, export cursor, write-mode slug and note-retire kind rejection). test/global-setup.ts:31 gates DB provisioning through canRunDbTests and :71 force-resets then replays partial indexes. Adversarial refine audit: enumerated all 129 original acceptance criteria against spec.md, retaining them as the first 15/17/17/12/11/13/9/7/7/7/14 entries respectively in US-001 through US-011; none was moved or dropped. Preserve every original qualifier, notably multi-byte exact-size validation, identical source/type restatement, FACT still-rendered triples, TTL/status eligibility, Chinese zero-match fallback, no-owner scope=user isolation, already-exported supersede replay, 300ms not-before and same-delay clearing, no-second-create policy patching, any-row grant refusal, and client-side updatedAt/faked-clock export verification. Important interface correction from fresh code reads: KodaPrincipal discriminates on actorType ('user', 'agent', 'runner'), while ToolContext.actor is already a user/agent principal; neither should be extended with a new uppercase type field (apps/api/src/auth/principal/koda-principal.types.ts:8,16,25; apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/assistant-tool.types.ts:21). Where the spec writes principal.type, treat it as normalized approval-subject notation: reuse ownerTypeFor(principal) / ownerTypeFor(ctx.actor) after the existing runner exclusion to produce USER or AGENT (apps/api/src/memory/memory-write.guard.ts:92). outOfScope: No pending memory rows and no `status: pending` value: proposal mode is a project approval policy on `memory.create` for AGENT principals (ruling 2026-11-03); an unapproved write simply does not exist yet.

Proposal mode covers `POST /memory`, `koda_add_memory` and `POST /memory/notes/:id/retire` only (all `memory.create`); `POST /memory/extract` (`memory.extract`) and `POST /memory/decisions` (`memory.decision.record`) keep their own policies and are not switched by the write-mode toggle.
No project column for the write mode; the mode is derived from approval policies on every read.
No org-wide memory, and no Agent-to-User ownership: a user-scoped item is owned by the principal that wrote it.
User scope is NOTE-only; triples (FACT, DECISION, PREFERENCE, CONSTRAINT, INCIDENT_PATTERN) stay project-scoped.
`POST /memory/:id/retire` stays decision-only; notes retire through `POST /memory/notes/:id/retire` (US-011). No soft delete or hard delete of notes is added.
US-011 only: no CLI command and no assistant or MCP tool retires a note; nax calls the REST route.
No hybrid vector plus keyword ranking; the knowledge base (LanceDB) stays the semantic layer.
`MemoryGovernanceService` (expire, downrank, dedupe, supersession), extraction, canonical state, review decisions and the `/context` builder are unchanged and never read user-scoped rows.
No MCP twin of the export route (`koda_memory_export`); HTTP is the only export surface.
Export and list responses are not fenced; fencing stays in the MCP tool text.
A user note written through project Q is visible to its owner in every project, including a proposal-mode project P that never held it for approval; per-project review of user notes is not added.
Full-text search uses the `english` configuration only; no Chinese segmentation is added (unsegmented text falls back to the substring match).
`.nax/rules/api-data.md` and other rule files are not edited by this feature.
